source: NOAA CPC weekly Niño indices (wksst9120), anomalies against 1991–2020

zones.name: Niño 4
zones.what: the western patch, over the warm pool

zones.name: Niño 3.4
zones.what: the patch El Niño is judged by

zones.name: Niño 1+2
zones.what: the coastal strip off Peru and Ecuador

chain.note: The order asked about — the centre first, then the east — is tested here as one sequence, not as six separate pairs: the four patches are sorted by the week each reached its own highest, and that order is compared with the geography.

overlap: Niño 3.4 (170–120°W) and Niño 3 (150–90°W) share 30° of longitude — 60 % of the width of 3.4 and half of 3. Niño 4 (160°E–150°W) and Niño 3.4 share 20°. Only Niño 1+2 (90–80°W) touches none of the others, which is why it is the only patch with a timing of its own.

skill.verdict: Even the best pair, Niño 1+2 into Niño 3 at 8 weeks, only changes the error by 0.011 °C in its favour — between -0.038 and +0.023 °C once the events are resampled. Against an index published to 0.1 °C that is nothing: a patch is not forecast by its neighbour, it is forecast by its own past. So this scene shows what happened before, not what will happen.

composite.formula: Niño 1+2 minus Niño 4, the same contrast the panel uses for the type of an event

subsurface.note: Temperature anomaly at 100 m along the equator, month by month. The mark is the centre of mass of the warm part, not a current: it also travels east when the west simply cools. The steps are months, so a speed read from them is a slope over months, not a measured current, and the same number is shown on Heat on the move.

note: Four patches of the same equator, measured at the surface. The panel can say which patch warmed first and how far the event leans east or centre; it cannot say that heat moved from one patch to another, because a surface temperature is not a flow of energy. Niño 3.4 and Niño 3 overlap between 150°W and 120°W, so part of what they share is the same water counted twice. The water that does move is below: the subsurface panel shows it, measured.
